From: Alex Darwin <alex.darwin@guardianpath.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Authorization & network constraints — GuardianPath onboarding

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to kick off Redwood for production. A couple of things we need to lock down before CS hands this to engineering:

- SSO: SAML IdP metadata will be provided, but we need the exact ACS and Entity IDs for your hosted endpoints.
- SCIM: We will provision groups from Okta; need supported SCIM attributes and any rate limits.
- IP allowlists: We operate from a small set of egress IPs per region; need to confirm whether we should whitelist per-tenant IPs or ranges for all traffic.
- Service accounts: We need patterns for machine/service identities that Redwood requires (least-privilege recommendations + rotation cadence).
- Org policies: Any platform-level defaults (session timeouts, retention) that will affect our compliance scope.

Attached is a short inventory we filled out (gp-saml-scim-inventory.xlsx). Can you confirm an initial list of requirements and the expected timeline for implementation? Procurement will need preliminary network/IP instructions to move to the next step.

Best,
Alex Darwin
Director, Platform Security
GuardianPath

--

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alex Darwin <alex.darwin@guardianpath.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Authorization & network constraints — GuardianPath onboarding

Alex — thanks for the clear inventory and the list. Looping in Ben (CS lead) and Irene (security/infra) so we can align the implementation plan. Quick answers and next steps below, and Ben will follow up with a formal handoff playbook.

Short answers:
- SSO/SAML: ACS & entity IDs for hosted customers are documented in our SSO guide; I'll attach the template we use so you can drop your IdP values. We also support multiple SP-initiated ACS endpoints for canary vs prod.
- SCIM: We support users and groups; primary attributes: userName, name, emails, groups (by id). Recommended rate limit for initial sync: 4 req/s per tenant; we can negotiate a window for a full backfill.
- IP allowlists: For the tightest security posture we recommend per-tenant static egress IPs (Dedicated) or a region-level allowlist for Hosted customers. Since you mentioned production, we should plan for per-tenant IPs via Dedicated or use static NAT ranges — I'll flag options.
- Service accounts: See attached patterns doc. Short version: two machine identities — "integration" (least privilege, short TTL) and "pipeline" (broader scope, rotated monthly).
- Org policies: Default retention is 90 days for debug logs; audit logs retained for 365 days (enterprise add-on available).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Ben will schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff with your infra team (proposed window: next Tue/Wed).
2) GuardianPath provides: SAML metadata, SCIM test account, and the egress IP ranges you want to allow.
3) Irene to validate network and service account patterns and propose a canary test plan.

Attachments: redwood-sso-scim-template.xlsx; ip-allowlist-guide.pdf

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: GuardianPath onboarding — implementation owners and questions

Irene / Soojin — following up internally. I'll run the customer kickoff and own the timeline, but need engineering validation on a few items before we lock dates:

1) Per-tenant egress IPs: what is the expected lead time to allocate and attach a static NAT range for a new Dedicated tenant? Any infra dependencies we should surface?
2) SCIM backfill: if GuardianPath requests a full group/user backfill (50k objects), do we want to throttle or provide a one-time elevated window? What's the rate-limit enforcement method?
3) SSO metadata edge cases: we occasionally see IdPs not provide group membership by default — what is our fallback?
4) Service account rotation: can we provide an automation hook for customers to rotate keys via an API call, or do we require manual operator action?

Irene — can you advise on 1/2/3 and add any operational constraints? I dropped a short doc with recommended service-account patterns into this thread (service-account-patterns.md).

Thanks — Ben

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Darwin <alex.darwin@guardianpath.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Authorization & network constraints — GuardianPath onboarding

On Thu, Aug 19, 2026 at 9:12 AM, Alex Darwin <alex.darwin@guardianpath.com> wrote:
> Hi Soojin,
> 
> Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to kick off Redwood for production. A couple of things we need to lock down before CS hands this to engineering:
> 
> - SSO: SAML IdP metadata will be provided, but we need the exact ACS and Entity IDs for your hosted endpoints.
> - SCIM: We will provision groups from Okta; need supported SCIM attributes and any rate limits.

Alex — quick technical notes from infra/security:

1) Per-tenant egress IPs: For Dedicated tenants we can reserve a /29 static NAT block; typical lead time is 5 business days from ticket creation. If GuardianPath needs Hosted + static egress we can propose a static NAT allocation at region level (longer lead time, ~10 business days).
2) SCIM backfill: We prefer to offer a one-time elevated window for large backfills. We'll set a temporary 20 req/s window for 2 hours (monitoring enabled) and ask CS to coordinate the scheduled time. Full syncs over 200k objects will need an engineering runbook.
3) SSO group fallback: if IdP does not provide group membership in assertions, we can map group membership via SCIM on first sync and then rely on SCIM for membership state. We need Okta to send group.membership or we use an attribute mapping.
4) Service account rotation: We expose a rotation API; operator approval only required for cross-tenant role changes. We'll provide the API spec in the implementation ticket.

Action items I need from GuardianPath to proceed:
- Confirm whether you're targeting Dedicated (per-tenant IP) or Hosted (region-level).
- Provide SAML metadata file and a SCIM test account with admin-level API token.
- Pick 2-hour windows where we can run the initial SCIM backfill (prefer 2–4am PT).

I'll open an internal implementation ticket and attach the runbook.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Security Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: (internal runbook added to ticket IMPL-298)
